stories.headline: Karnataka Cabinet clears Bill allowing 5% park land for public projects
stories.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears Bill allowing 5% park land for public projects
stories.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved a Bill to amend the Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, allowing portions of park and garden land to be used for public infrastructure and utility projects, a move opposed by the BJP on environmental grounds. Sources said the Cabinet, which met on Friday, approved the proposed amendments to the Act, which governs prominent Bengaluru green spaces, including Cubbon Park and Lalbagh. Under the amendment, up to five per cent of the total extent of any park or garden can be alienated for specified public purposes through sale, lease, gift, exchange or mortgage. Only government departments, statutory authorities, state-owned companies and local authorities would be permitted to use the alienated portions for public infrastructure or utility projects, according to the proposed legislation. stories.headline: Bangladesh-Pakistan ties: What Dhaka’s interest in Saudi-Türkiye defence pact means for India
stories.title: Bangladesh-Pakistan ties: What Dhaka’s interest in Saudi-Türkiye defence pact means for India
stories.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs has said it is closely following developments surrounding the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence arrangement and is examining their implications for India's national security, regional peace and stability.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in summary weight 42
article_sentences: The development marks a striking shift in South Asian geopolitics.
It also presents a new challenge for India, which has traditionally enjoyed much closer strategic and security ties with Bangladesh than Pakistan has.

Humayun Kabir, foreign affairs adviser to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has said Dhaka has a positive approach towards potentially joining an economic or defence framework involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye.
Kabir stressed that Bangladesh's policy is guided by a “Bangladesh First” approach and that Dhaka is pursuing a balanced foreign policy based on national interests.
He also said Bangladesh was strengthening its working relationship with Pakistan, particularly in trade and people-to-people connectivity.
The statement does not mean Bangladesh has formally joined the pact.
Rather, Dhaka has indicated that it is open to the possibility.

The Ministry of External Affairs has said it is closely following developments surrounding the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence arrangement and is examining their implications for India's national security, regional peace and stability.
Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye have signed a joint defence agreement designed around collective deterrence.
